_doc: Oathwild's own combat knobs (js/rules/combat.js is the one reader). Damage maths is Farhold's (rpg.strike); these are the world sim's timings, ranges, stamina costs and death rules.

aimAssist._doc: How far off the aim line (degrees) a target-an-ally or beam spell still finds someone.

stamina._doc: Stamina pays for sprint (per second), a dodge roll, a power attack (a held swing) and every hit you block.

combatState._doc: A body is 'in combat' while a monster has it on its threat list or it hit or was hit in the last `seconds`.

regen._doc: Out of combat, share of maximum health and mana back per second (in combat only the sheet's own regen).

death._doc: A player at 0 health is downed for `downedSeconds` (an ally can revive them by holding Interact for `reviveSeconds` within `reviveRange`, back at `reviveShare` health); after that, or by choice, they respawn at their last shrine paying `goldShare` of their gold (at most goldCapPerLevel x level) and inventory.json durability.respawnLoss.

xpRange._doc: Players further than this from a kill get no XP or loot from it (they did not help, or wandered off).

pets._doc: Summoned companions: their health/damage come from their monster row at the caster's level, x the summon's power and the caster's petPct.

monsterScale._doc: Oathwild's monsters live longer than Farhold's (owner: WoW-like fights). x on every monster's health and damage at spawn (companions are not scaled).

farholdEnemies._doc: Laid over farhold/data/balance.json `enemies` in memory (js/rules/engine.js): how fast a monster's health and damage grow per level. Oathwild's characters grow faster per level than Farhold's (class points, ranks, class depth), so its monsters do too.

magicWeapon._doc: A magic weapon attacks with spell power in its own style (js/rules/casters.js, data/casters.json): `mult` is every style's base share (a style's own share multiplies it); `element` and `range` are the plain bolt of a quarterstaff or an orb left in the main hand.

formSwing._doc: Seconds between a shape's basic attacks (a wolf's bite, a bear's swipe) before haste; each attack lands the shape's `hits`.
